title: Single Number
statement_short: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single element. You must implement a solution with linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 3 \* 10^4, -3 \* 10^4 <= nums[i] <= 3 \* 10^4, every element appears twice except for one
hint: Strict linear time and O(1) extra space constraints call for Bitwise XOR to cancel out paired duplicate numbers.
why_not: Right: Bit Manipulation applies XOR accumulator (a ^ a = 0) to eliminate duplicate pairs in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Frequency counting in a set/map finds the single number in O(n) time, but consumes O(n) extra space, violating O(1). Not Sorting: Sorting elements adjacent pairs takes O(n log n) time, violating linear time requirements. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointer pairs requires sorted array ordering, taking O(n log n) total time.
